passages.text: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the kingdom of heaven.
He said the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins.
These ten virgins each took a lamp.
They went out to meet the bridegroom.
passages.original: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου

passages.text: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a story about the kingdom of heaven.
He said there were ten virgins.
Each virgin had a lamp.
Five virgins were foolish.
Five virgins were wise.
passages.original: πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι

passages.text: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.
passages.sermon: Five of the virgins were foolish.\r\nThese foolish virgins took their lamps.\r\nThey did not take extra oil with them.
passages.original: αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον

passages.text: But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.
passages.sermon:
The wise virgins acted with understanding.
They took oil with them.
They put the oil in flasks.
They carried the flasks with their lamps.
passages.original: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
passages.sermon: The bridegroom was delayed.\r\nAll the virgins became drowsy.\r\nAll the virgins fell asleep.
passages.original: χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον

passages.text: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’
passages.sermon:
It was midnight.
A loud cry rang out.
Someone said, “Here is the bridegroom!”
They called everyone to come out.
They said, “Come out to meet him!”
passages.original: Μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.
passages.sermon: All the virgins were waiting for the bridegroom.\r\nThey all woke up.\r\nEach virgin prepared her lamp.
passages.original: Τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’
passages.sermon:
There were ten virgins waiting for the bridegroom.
Some virgins were foolish.
Some virgins were wise.
The foolish virgins spoke to the wise virgins.
The foolish virgins said, “Give us some of your oil.”
The foolish virgins said, “Our lamps are going out.”
passages.original: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται

passages.text: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’
passages.sermon:
The wise virgins answered the foolish virgins.
The wise virgins said, "No."
They said, "There may not be enough oil for us and for you."
They said, "Go to those who sell oil."
They said, "Buy oil for yourselves."
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι Μή¦Ποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς

passages.text: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
passages.sermon:
The bridegroom arrived.
The foolish virgins were away buying oil.
The wise virgins were ready.
The wise virgins went in with the bridegroom.
They entered the wedding banquet.
Someone shut the door.
passages.original: Ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετ’ αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα

passages.text: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’
passages.sermon: The other virgins came later.\r\nThey arrived after the door was shut.\r\nThey said, "Lord, Lord, open the door for us!"
passages.original: Ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι Κύριε κύριε ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν

passages.text: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
passages.sermon: The bridegroom answered them.\r\nHe said, “Truly, I tell you.\r\nI do not know you.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He warned them to stay alert.
He said, "You do not know the day."
He said, "You do not know the hour."
Therefore, keep watch.
passages.original: Γρηγορεῖτε οὖν ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν

passages.text: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a story about a man.
This man planned to go on a journey.
He called his own servants to him.
He gave his possessions to his servants.
He trusted his servants with what belonged to him.
passages.original: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent—each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.
passages.sermon:
A man went on a journey.
He called his servants.
He gave one servant five talents.
He gave another servant two talents.
He gave another servant one talent.
He gave each servant a different amount.
He gave to each according to that servant’s own ability.
Then the man left on his journey.
passages.original: καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν

passages.text: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.
passages.sermon:
A man went on a journey.
He called his servants.
He gave his possessions to them.
He gave one servant five talents.
This servant received five talents.
He went at once.
He put the five talents to work.
He gained five more talents.
passages.original: Εὐθέως Πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα πέντε

passages.text: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.
passages.sermon: The servant received two talents from his master.\r\nThis servant worked with the two talents.\r\nHe gained two more talents.
passages.original: ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο

passages.text: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.
passages.sermon:
A servant received one talent from his master.
This servant went away.
He dug a hole in the ground.
He hid his master’s money in the hole.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν γῆν καὶ ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After a long time the master of those servants returned to settle accounts with them.
passages.sermon:
The master had several servants.
A long time passed.
The master returned.
He came to those servants.
He wanted to settle accounts with them.
He met with them to review what they had done.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ πολὺν χρόνον ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει λόγον μετ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’
passages.sermon:
A servant received five talents from his master.
This servant came to his master.
He brought five more talents with him.
He spoke to his master.
He said, “Master, you gave me five talents.
See, I have gained five more talents.”
passages.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων Κύριε πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα

passages.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to his servant.
The master said, "Well done."
The master called the servant good.
The master called the servant faithful.
The servant was faithful with a few things.
The master said, "I will put you in charge of many things."
The master said, "Enter into the joy of your master."
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ Εὖ δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου

passages.text: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’
passages.sermon:
A servant received two talents from his master.
This servant came to his master.
He spoke to his master.
He said, “Master, you gave me two talents.
See, I have gained two more talents.”
passages.original: Προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο τάλαντα εἶπεν Κύριε δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα

passages.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to his servant.
The master said, "Well done."
The master called the servant good and faithful.
The servant had been faithful with a few things.
The master promised to put the servant in charge of many things.
The master invited the servant to enter into his joy.
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ Εὖ δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου

passages.text: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.
passages.sermon:
A servant came to his master.
This servant had received one talent from his master.
The servant spoke to his master.
He said, "Master, I knew you are a hard man."
"You reap where you have not sown."
"You gather where you have not scattered seed."
passages.original: Προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν Κύριε ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας

passages.text: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’
passages.sermon:
The servant felt afraid.
He went away.
He hid his master’s talent in the ground.
He returned the talent to his master.
He said, “Here is what belongs to you.”
passages.original: καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν

passages.text: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to his servant.
The master called him wicked.
The master called him lazy.
The master said, "You knew this about me."
The master said, "I reap where I have not sown."
The master said, "I gather where I have not scattered seed."
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα

passages.text: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.
passages.sermon: The master spoke to his servant.\r\nThe master said the servant should have put his money with the bankers.\r\nThe master said he would have received his money back with interest when he returned.
passages.original: ἔδει σε οὖν βαλεῖν τὰ ἀργύριά μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ

passages.text: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to his servants.
He said, "Take the talent away from this servant."
He said, "Give the talent to the servant who has ten talents."
The master gave the talent to the one who already had ten talents.
passages.original: Ἄρατε οὖν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα

passages.text: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the kingdom of heaven.
He explained how God rewards faithfulness.
Everyone who has will receive more.
He will have plenty.
But anyone who does not have will lose even what he has.
God gives more to those who use what they have well.
God takes away from those who do not use what they have.
passages.original: τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται τοῦ δὲ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the final judgment.
He described a servant.
This servant was worthless.
He did not use what his master gave him.
Jesus said, "Throw this worthless servant out."
Send him into the outer darkness.
In that place, people will weep.
They will gnash their teeth.
passages.original: καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων

passages.text: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on His glorious throne.
passages.sermon:
The Son of Man is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ will come again.
He will come in His glory.
All the angels will come with Him.
Jesus will sit on His glorious throne.
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ

passages.text: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
He will come in His glory.
All the angels will come with Him.
He will sit on His glorious throne.
All the nations will gather before Jesus.
Jesus will separate the people from each other.
He will do this like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
passages.original: καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων

passages.text: He will place the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
He will come in His glory.
All the angels will come with Him.
He will sit on His glorious throne.
He will gather all the nations before Him.
He will separate the people from each other.
He will act like a shepherd.
A shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
Jesus will place the sheep on His right.
He will place the goats on His left.
passages.original: καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων

passages.text: Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
passages.sermon:
The King stands before all the nations.
He speaks to the people on His right.
These people are like sheep separated by the shepherd.
The King says, "Come."
He calls them blessed by His Father.
He tells them to inherit the kingdom.
This kingdom was prepared for them.
God prepared it from the foundation of the world.
passages.original: Τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ Δεῦτε οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου

passages.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in, I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you visited Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King.
Jesus speaks to the people on His right.
Jesus says what they did for Him.
I was hungry.
You gave Me food.
I was thirsty.
You gave Me something to drink.
I was a stranger.
You welcomed Me.
I was naked.
You clothed Me.
I was sick.
You cared for Me.
I was in prison.
You visited Me.
passages.original: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με

passages.text: Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?
passages.sermon:
The righteous people will answer the King.
They will speak to Him.
They will say, “Lord, when did we see You hungry?
When did we feed You?
When did we see You thirsty?
When did we give You something to drink?”
passages.original: Τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες Κύριε πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν

passages.text: When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?
passages.sermon:
The righteous people speak to the King.
They ask Him a question.
They say, “Lord, when did we see You as a stranger and welcome You?”
They also say, “When did we see You without clothes and give You clothing?”
passages.original: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν

passages.text: When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’
passages.sermon:
The righteous people speak to Jesus.
They ask Him a question.
They say, “Lord, when did we see You sick?
When did we see You in prison?
When did we come to visit You?”
passages.original: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε

passages.text: And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King.
Jesus will answer them.
Jesus will say, “Truly, I tell you this.
Whatever you did for one of the least of My brothers,
you did for Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε

passages.text: Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King and Judge.
He will speak to the people on His left.
He will say, “Go away from Me.”
He will call them cursed.
He will send them into the eternal fire.
God prepared this fire for the devil.
God also prepared it for the devil’s angels.
passages.original: Τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων Πορεύεσθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink, I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King.
Jesus speaks to those on His left.
Jesus says what they did not do for Him.
I was hungry.
You did not give Me food.
I was thirsty.
You did not give Me anything to drink.
I was a stranger.
You did not welcome Me.
I was naked.
You did not clothe Me.
I was sick.
I was in prison.
You did not visit Me.
passages.original: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν καὶ ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με

passages.text: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’
passages.sermon:
The people on the left will answer Jesus.
They will say, "Lord, when did we see You hungry?"
They will say, "When did we see You thirsty?"
They will say, "When did we see You as a stranger?"
They will say, "When did we see You naked?"
They will say, "When did we see You sick?"
They will say, "When did we see You in prison?"
They will say, "When did we not serve You?"
passages.original: Τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες Κύριε πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι

passages.text: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King.
Jesus will answer them.
Jesus will say, “Truly, I tell you this.
Whatever you did not do for one of the least of these people,
you did not do for Me.”
passages.original: Τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε

passages.text: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke about the final judgment.\r\nHe said some people will go away into eternal punishment.\r\nHe said the righteous will go into eternal life.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον
